title: Gastrointestinal Stromal Tumor Cancer
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE navigator (draft)
provenanceNote: DRAFT decision support authored from standard guidelines (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison) - physician decides.
sourceNote: Structural pathway consistent with standard oncology references for GIST (NCCN/DeVita/Harrison). Original wording. Systemic-therapy leaves reference existing StewardMD Standard Protocols; the dose engine computes patient doses. No proprietary guideline text reproduced.

a.text: Risk of recurrence is estimated from tumor size, mitotic rate (per 5 sq mm / 50 HPF) and primary site; non-gastric (small bowel, rectal) sites carry higher risk at equal size and mitotic count.

b.text: For resected high-risk KIT-mutant GIST, adjuvant imatinib for at least 3 years improves recurrence-free and overall survival versus shorter courses.

c.text: PDGFRA exon 18 D842V mutation is intrinsically resistant to imatinib; avapritinib is the preferred agent. Imatinib adjuvant therapy offers no benefit here.

d.text: Mutation testing (KIT / PDGFRA, and SDH where indicated) should precede any systemic decision, since genotype predicts TKI sensitivity and starting dose.

nodes.name: Initial workup
nodes.title: Initial workup and diagnosis
nodes.description: Confirm GIST histology, define extent, and obtain molecular status before any treatment decision.

bullets.label: History, exam, performance status; GI bleeding / mass symptoms
Contrast CT of abdomen and pelvis; chest imaging for staging
Biopsy with immunohistochemistry
bullets.sub: CD117 (KIT) and/or DOG1 positive; assess mitotic rate per 5 sq mm

bullets.label: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided biopsy for gastric / esophagogastric lesions when feasible
Molecular testing before systemic therapy
bullets.sub: KIT (exons 9, 11, 13, 17), PDGFRA (exon 18 incl. D842V); SDHB IHC if KIT/PDGFRA wild-type

bullets.label: Multidisciplinary review with a sarcoma / GIST-experienced team

nodes.name: Clinical presentation
nodes.title: Clinical presentation / disease state
nodes.description: Choose the current clinical state; this selects the pathway (localized surgery vs systemic vs recurrence / surveillance).

nodes.name: Resectability
nodes.title: Localized: resectability assessment
nodes.description: Decide whether complete (R0) resection is achievable now with acceptable function-preserving morbidity.
bullets: Tumors < 2 cm without high-risk EUS features may be observed with periodic endoscopy
Consider neoadjuvant TKI when downsizing would allow organ preservation (e.g. GE junction, duodenum, low rectum)

options.label: Very small (< 2 cm) incidental gastric, no high-risk EUS features
Marginally resectable - would benefit from downsizing

nodes.name: Small tumor - observe
nodes.title: Very small incidental gastric GIST: endoscopic surveillance
nodes.description: Sub-2 cm gastric GIST without high-risk features may be followed rather than resected.
bullets: Periodic endoscopic ultrasound to track size and echofeatures
Resect on growth, symptoms, or new high-risk features (irregular margin, cystic spaces, heterogeneity)
Shared decision-making; resection is reasonable if surveillance is impractical

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant mutation status
nodes.title: Marginally resectable: mutation-directed neoadjuvant plan
nodes.description: Genotype predicts whether neoadjuvant imatinib will shrink the tumor before surgery.

nodes.name: Neoadjuvant imatinib
nodes.title: Neoadjuvant imatinib then surgery
nodes.description: Imatinib to maximal response, then function-preserving resection.
bullets: Imatinib until best radiologic response (typically 6-12 months), monitored by CT with response assessment
Operate at maximal response - do not wait for progression
Continue imatinib perioperatively; resume adjuvant course after recovery based on residual risk
Confirm KIT sensitivity on molecular report before starting

nodes.name: Resistant genotype - surgery
nodes.title: Resistant genotype: proceed to surgery
nodes.description: Imatinib is unlikely to downsize a D842V / resistant tumor; plan surgery directly.
bullets: Proceed to resection if achievable; neoadjuvant imatinib offers no benefit for D842V
For PDGFRA D842V requiring downsizing, consider avapritinib in a trial / expert setting (no dose protocol here - guidance only)
Re-stage and re-assess resectability after multidisciplinary review

nodes.name: Recurrence-risk stratification
nodes.title: Resected localized GIST: recurrence-risk stratification
nodes.description: After complete resection, estimate recurrence risk from size, mitotic rate and site to decide on adjuvant therapy.

tables.title: Risk of recurrence by size, mitotic rate and site (approximate)

nodes.name: Low risk - observe
nodes.title: Very-low / low risk: surveillance, no adjuvant therapy
nodes.description: Complete resection with low recurrence risk; adjuvant TKI is not indicated.
bullets: No adjuvant imatinib
History, exam and abdominopelvic CT every 6 months for 5 years, then annually
Return to the recurrence pathway on any new lesion

nodes.name: Intermediate risk
nodes.title: Intermediate risk: individualize adjuvant therapy
nodes.description: Adjuvant imatinib is discretionary; weigh site, mutation and patient factors.
bullets: Discuss adjuvant imatinib for non-gastric primaries or tumor rupture, where risk approaches the high-risk group
Confirm KIT sensitivity before any adjuvant TKI; PDGFRA D842V derives no benefit
If adjuvant imatinib is chosen, use the referenced protocol; otherwise proceed to surveillance
CT abdomen / pelvis every 3-6 months for the first years

nodes.name: Adjuvant mutation status
nodes.title: High risk: mutation-directed adjuvant decision
nodes.description: Adjuvant benefit depends on genotype; select the mutation class.

nodes.name: Adjuvant imatinib (KIT ex11)
nodes.title: High risk, KIT exon 11: adjuvant imatinib >= 3 years
nodes.description: Standard adjuvant therapy for the most imatinib-sensitive genotype.
bullets: Adjuvant imatinib for at least 3 years
Standard starting dose; monitor tolerance and adherence
Surveillance CT during and after therapy
Longer duration is under study for the highest-risk cases

nodes.name: Adjuvant imatinib (KIT ex9)
nodes.title: High risk, KIT exon 9: adjuvant imatinib (dose consideration)
nodes.description: Exon 9 tumors are imatinib-sensitive but may need a higher dose; adjuvant course still >= 3 years.
bullets: Adjuvant imatinib for at least 3 years
Exon 9 disease may warrant a higher daily dose - the dose engine computes the patient's dose
Monitor for the added toxicity of higher dosing
Surveillance CT during and after therapy

nodes.name: D842V - no adjuvant
nodes.title: PDGFRA D842V: no adjuvant imatinib, surveillance
nodes.description: D842V is imatinib-resistant; adjuvant imatinib is not indicated.
bullets: No adjuvant imatinib - the genotype predicts resistance
Close surveillance CT; enter the metastatic pathway if disease recurs (avapritinib is the active agent for D842V)
Refer to a GIST expert center where available

nodes.name: Wild-type / SDH-deficient
nodes.title: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type or SDH-deficient: surveillance / referral
nodes.description: Adjuvant imatinib is generally not beneficial for wild-type / SDH-deficient GIST.
bullets: Adjuvant imatinib is not routinely recommended - limited benefit in wild-type / SDH-deficient disease
Refer to an expert center; consider SDH-deficient / syndromic workup (Carney triad, NF1) as indicated
Surveillance CT / MRI on an individualized schedule

nodes.name: Metastatic mutation status
nodes.title: Unresectable / metastatic: first-line by genotype
nodes.description: Genotype selects the first-line agent and starting dose for advanced GIST.

nodes.name: Wild-type subtype
nodes.title: Wild-type GIST: sub-classification
nodes.description: KIT/PDGFRA wild-type GIST is heterogeneous; sub-classification changes workup and referral.
bullets: SDH-deficient (SDHB IHC loss): younger patients, gastric, multifocal; Carney triad / Carney-Stratakis
NF1-associated or BRAF-mutant: distinct biology and drug sensitivity

nodes.name: SDH-deficient GIST
nodes.title: SDH-deficient GIST: expert referral, individualized therapy
nodes.description: SDH-deficient disease is typically TKI-refractory and indolent; manage at an expert center.
bullets: Refer to a sarcoma expert center; consider genetic counseling (SDHx germline, Carney triad / Carney-Stratakis)
Standard KIT-targeted TKIs are usually ineffective; sunitinib or regorafenib may give some benefit
Enroll in a clinical trial where available; surgery for symptomatic / oligometastatic disease
Often indolent - a watchful approach can be appropriate

nodes.name: First-line imatinib (KIT ex11)
nodes.title: Metastatic, KIT exon 11: first-line imatinib
nodes.description: Imatinib is standard first-line for advanced KIT-mutant GIST; continue until progression or intolerance.
bullets: Imatinib continuously until progression or unacceptable toxicity
Assess response by CT; a decrease in density can indicate response even without shrinkage
Consider resection of residual / oligometastatic disease at best response in selected patients
On progression, re-assess and enter the progression pathway

nodes.name: First-line imatinib (KIT ex9)
nodes.title: Metastatic, KIT exon 9: first-line imatinib (higher dose)
nodes.description: Exon 9 disease responds to imatinib, generally at a higher daily dose.
bullets: Imatinib first-line; exon 9 tumors often benefit from a higher daily dose - the dose engine computes it
Monitor the additional toxicity of higher dosing
Continue until progression, then enter the progression pathway

nodes.name: First-line avapritinib (D842V)
nodes.title: Metastatic, PDGFRA D842V: avapritinib
nodes.description: D842V is imatinib-resistant; avapritinib is the preferred agent.
bullets: Avapritinib for PDGFRA exon 18 D842V-mutant advanced GIST
No dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; the physician arranges the regimen
Monitor for cognitive effects and intracranial bleeding per label
Do not use imatinib for D842V

nodes.name: Metastatic wild-type
nodes.title: Metastatic, wild-type / SDH-deficient: trial / referral
nodes.description: Wild-type and SDH-deficient GIST are often TKI-refractory; refer and consider trials.
bullets: Refer to a GIST expert center; enroll in a clinical trial where possible
A trial of imatinib or sunitinib may be considered, though responses are limited
For SDH-deficient disease, consider syndromic evaluation and specialized management
Multikinase TKIs (e.g. sunitinib, regorafenib) are options on progression

nodes.name: Progression / line of therapy
nodes.title: Metastatic progression: sequencing of TKIs
nodes.description: Advanced GIST is treated by sequential TKI lines. Select the line reached at progression.
bullets: Confirm true progression (RECIST / density change); rule out non-adherence before switching
Consider resection or ablation of focal / limited progression while continuing the same TKI

options.label: Limited / focal progression (rest of disease controlled)

nodes.name: Focal progression
nodes.title: Limited progression: local therapy, continue TKI
nodes.description: For focal progression with otherwise controlled disease, treat the progressing site and stay on the same TKI.
bullets: Resection, ablation (RFA), or radiotherapy to the progressing lesion
Continue the current TKI - most disease remains sensitive
Switch to the next systemic line only when progression becomes generalized
Confirm adherence and rule out pseudo-progression before acting

nodes.name: Second-line sunitinib
nodes.title: Post-imatinib: second-line sunitinib
nodes.description: Standard second-line therapy after imatinib failure or intolerance.
bullets: Sunitinib after imatinib progression / intolerance
Before switching, consider imatinib dose escalation for exon 9 or limited progression
Monitor blood pressure, thyroid function, hand-foot syndrome
On progression, advance to third-line therapy

nodes.name: Third-line regorafenib
nodes.title: Post-sunitinib: third-line regorafenib
nodes.description: Standard third-line therapy after imatinib and sunitinib.
bullets: Regorafenib after progression on imatinib and sunitinib
Monitor blood pressure, hand-foot skin reaction, and liver function
On progression, advance to fourth-line therapy

nodes.name: Fourth-line ripretinib
nodes.title: Post-regorafenib: fourth-line ripretinib
nodes.description: Fourth-line switch-control TKI after three prior lines.
bullets: Ripretinib after imatinib, sunitinib and regorafenib
No dose protocol here yet - shown as guidance; the physician arranges the regimen
Consider a clinical trial or rechallenge with a prior TKI for palliation if no trial available
Continue best supportive care throughout

nodes.name: Recurrence pattern
nodes.title: Recurrence after resection
nodes.description: Distinguish resectable local recurrence from disseminated disease.
bullets: Re-image (CT chest/abdomen/pelvis) and re-confirm mutation status if not already known
Most recurrences are treated as advanced disease with systemic TKI

nodes.name: Resect recurrence
nodes.title: Isolated recurrence: resection + systemic therapy
nodes.description: Resection of isolated recurrence, usually combined with a TKI.
bullets: Resect isolated recurrence when complete removal is feasible
Start / resume imatinib for KIT-sensitive disease - most recurrent GIST is treated as advanced disease
Enter surveillance after treatment

nodes.name: Surveillance
nodes.title: Post-treatment surveillance
nodes.description: Follow-up cadence after resection or during / after systemic therapy.
bullets: After resection of higher-risk GIST: CT abdomen / pelvis every 3-6 months for 3-5 years, then annually to 10 years
Low-risk resected GIST: less frequent imaging, individualized
On systemic therapy: periodic CT with response assessment; watch for progression to change lines
Any new lesion returns to the recurrence / progression pathway
